goal: Help the developer install the Visual Studio components that expose current WinUI 3 project templates.
must_include: Says the missing template is an installation/workload issue, not a project-file problem.
Tells them to modify Visual Studio and install the current WinUI/Windows application development workload or the Windows App SDK template components for their Visual Studio version.
Mentions restarting Visual Studio after modifying the installation so the templates are reloaded.
For older Visual Studio 2022 layouts, distinguishes the C# template component from the C++ template component instead of assuming one covers both languages.
must_not: Tell them to create a UWP project and later convert it to WinUI 3.
Tell them to fix this by editing the solution or adding a NuGet package to an empty project.
Require a command-line-only workflow when they are asking about Visual Studio templates.
acceptable_alternatives: Use the Visual Studio Installer Modify flow.
Use a Visual Studio configuration file or winget configuration that installs the same workload/components.
Use the Microsoft Learn WinUI quickstart's Visual Studio setup instructions for the installed Visual Studio generation.
solved: The answer names the missing Visual Studio workload/template components and gives a path to install them so WinUI 3 templates appear.
partial: The answer recognizes that Visual Studio components are missing but does not specify the workload/template components or version caveat.
notes: The Stack Overflow accepted answer describes the older Windows App SDK VSIX/template setup; current Microsoft Learn pages name a WinUI/Windows application development workload. Either is acceptable when matched to the Visual Studio version in the answer.
